title: Avoid flattening lists with sum
why: Using an empty list as the start value for sum repeatedly copies the accumulated list and makes flattening quadratic in the total output size.
suggestion: Use itertools.chain.from_iterable or a nested list comprehension to flatten the input in linear time.
limitations: Only calls named sum whose second positional argument or start keyword is a literal empty list are reported.
Shadowing of the Python built-in and the element types produced by the iterable are not resolved.
